name: CloudCannon
title: Mica vs. CloudCannon
summary: CloudCannon is a commercial managed CMS with visual editing, roles, support and DAM integrations. Mica is a free, experimental tool that you run yourself. The trade-off is control and simplicity against managed workflows; CloudCannon suits teams that want a supported service for their editors.

chooseMica.text: You want open source under the MIT licence, with no vendor service and no per-user price.
You want to run the editor yourself, on your machine or as a container behind any OpenID Connect provider.
You want the content model in TypeScript, with types in Astro Content Collections.
You want the real Astro page beside the form, with one integration, `micaPreview()`, and no `data-editable` attributes in your templates.
You want an MCP server built in, so agents save drafts under the same checks as an editor.

chooseOther.text: Editors should edit text and images on the page itself, and see components re-render as they edit.
You want a hosted service with support.
Your editors need roles with permission groups, and approval through a pull request.
You need SAML sign-in, or media in a DAM such as S3, Cloudinary or Bynder.
You want deploy previews of pull requests.
